outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenneth Walker earned his big salary in his Kansas City debut, rumbling for a career-high 173 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries while catching three of six targets for 18 yards and another score in a season-opening win over the Broncos. It was the kind of volume Walker rarely garnered in Seattle, but the fifth-year RB is being counted on to handle bell-cow duties with his new team, as rookie Emmett Johnson figures to be his primary backup for most or all of the season. Walker will aim to keep rolling in Week 2 against a Colts defense that just got steamrolled by Derrick Henry, but which ranked 11th in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenneth Walker didn't need a ceiling game in Kansas City's Week 3 win over the Dolphins. While he failed to reach 100 rushing yards for the first time this season, he did score his second rushing and second receiving touchdown of the year. Walker's addition has supercharged the entire offense, and he's thriving in a bell-cow role, amassing 360 rushing yards in three games while averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He's also on pace for a career-best campaign as a pass catcher. Walker could face a test in Week 4 against a Raiders defense that is tied for 10th in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs and has given up just one touchdown to the position so far in 2026.

player.seasonOutlook: Walker signed with the Chiefs after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Seahawks. The reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded running back from 2025, Walker is poised for feature-back duties in a good, Andy Reid-led offense. Having worked in a committee most of last season, Walker was limited to only five touchdowns and 11.3 fantasy points per game (both career lows), but he still generated 252 touches and a career-high 1,309 yards. He has yet to finish a season better than 18th in fantasy points (12th on a per-game basis) and has missed at least two games in three of four seasons in the league, but the 25-year-old's ability to contribute at a high level as a rusher and receiver is enough to position him as, at least, a fringe RB1 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylen Waddle did not contribute much in his Broncos' debut, catching just one of three targets for a meager two yards in the Week 1 loss to Kansas City. Steve Spagnuolo's rebuilt secondary prioritized taking Waddle out of the picture, and the former Dolphin wideout hasn't yet established enough chemistry with QB Bo Nix to overcome consistent double teams. Waddle will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jaylen Waddle is struggling to adjust to his new offense with the Broncos. The former Dolphins wide receiver caught only two of his seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams for 10 yards, while adding a 14-yard run. Waddle leads Denver with 20 targets through three games, but he's turned them into just 11 catches for 150 yards, and he's still looking for his first TD of the season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Waddle was traded to Denver after spending his first five seasons in Miami. The 2021 first-round pick was solid during his Dolphins tenure, finishing in the top 30 among receivers in fantasy PPG four times, though never reaching the top 10 while often playing second fiddle to Tyreek Hill. Although he has been a reliable target and has missed only seven games in five years, Waddle hasn't finished a season higher than 20th in targets or catches since 2021. In Denver, the 27-year-old Waddle will compete with Courtland Sutton for the team lead in targets in a scheme that likes to spread the ball around. Not utilized near the goal line much at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds (he's yet to clear seven end zone targets in a season), Waddle is likely to max out as a back-end WR2 in Denver.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyle Monangai will look to be a big contributor once again for the Bears in Week 2 against the Vikings. While Monangai still took a back-seat role to D'Andre Swift in Week 1 against the Panthers, he still finished the game with 10 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown, along with 24 yards off two catches. The second-year ball carrier should still have plenty of a share in Chicago's rushing game to be fantasy relevant, especially given how much potential their offense showed for the season. Monangai will face a Minnesota defense that shelled Green Bay on the ground in their opener, but the Bears have a much superior RB room as of now.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded 216 rushing yards to RBs this season, a bottom-10 mark in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyle Monangai should remain the complementary option in Chicago's backfield in Week 4 against the Jets. Monangai logged his third straight showing with 10 carries in Week 3 versus the Eagles, but he converted them for a season-low 31 rushing yards. The second-year running back also garnered no targets in the passing game, which came as a letdown after he posted a 4-35-0 receiving line leading up to the Monday Night win. He'll look to improve on his consistent volume against a New York defense that's allowed an eighth-most 24.1 fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Monangai heads into his second NFL season following an impressive rookie campaign in which he quickly forced his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The 2025 seventh-round flier played 41% of Chicago's offensive snaps and averaged a healthy 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts. Monangai was limited to 7.7 fantasy PPG during the 16 weeks Swift also played, but he showed his insurance value with a 29-touch, 198-yard effort in the one game Swift was sidelined (Week 9). The 24-year-old could see a slight boost in usage this season, but that usage and production will be limited as long as Swift is also healthy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Puka Nacua managed to put up decent numbers despite the Rams' dismal offensive performance in their season opener, and he'll look to ramp up his production further in Week 2 against the Giants. Nacua recorded 74 of Matthew Stafford's 155 passing yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco, though he caught just five of nine targets. No other Rams pass catcher had more than three catches or 26 yards, so there's little doubt that Nacua unsurprisingly remains Stafford's favorite target. The Giants' defense looked good in a win over Dallas in Week 1, with top wideout CeeDee Lamb posting a modest 5-44-1 receiving line.
outlooksByWeek.3: Puka Nacua (hip) is uncertain to play in the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Nacua missed Monday's Week 2 game versus the Giants, though he wasn't ruled out until game day. That lends some hope that Nacua could return soon, though his availability for practice during the week should provide more insight about his potential to return versus the Broncos. Should Nacua suit up, he'll draw a tough Denver secondary that have given up just 203 receiving yards to wideouts so far, tied for third-fewest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Puka Nacua (hip) could return to action when the Rams face Philadelphia in Week 4. Nacua has missed Los Angeles' past two games due to a hip injury, but there is some hope that he can return against the Eagles. While Nacua has been out, Davante Adams has thrived statistically as the Rams' top wideout. The team's receiving corps as a whole could find success against an Eagles squad that ranks 24th in the NFL through three weeks by giving up an average of 24.0 fantasy points per game to wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Nacua has defied the odds, emerging from fifth-round flier in 2023 to one of the most relied upon and productive offensive players in the league. Nacua has finished each of his three pro seasons sixth or better among receivers in fantasy PPG and peaked with a first-place finish last season. Matthew Stafford's top target led the league with 129 receptions and finished no lower than third among receivers in targets, yardage and touchdowns, while also adding 105 yards and one score as a rusher. More goal-line work would be nice (he has 11 end zone targets over the past two seasons), but Nacua's heavy usage in an elite offense locks in the 25-year-old as arguably the top receiver in fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: Matthew Stafford and the Rams will look to bounce back from a rough season-opening loss when they face the Giants in Week 2. Stafford threw for just 155 yards with no TDs and one interception against San Francisco last Thursday. He did still manage to connect with favorite target Puka Nacua five times for 74 yards, but no other Rams pass catcher had more than 26 yards in the defeat. A matchup with the Giants awaits, but New York had good results against Dallas' passing game in Week 1, holding QB Dak Prescott to 175 yards with one interception, albeit with two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Matthew Stafford will look to help guide the Rams to a much-needed win in Week 4 against Philadelphia following a disappointing 1-2 start to the season. Stafford threw for 390 yards and two touchdowns in Week 3 against Denver, but he also tossed two costly interceptions, including a pick-six. The reigning NFL MVP already has four interceptions on his ledger through three contests after logging just eight interceptions across 17 regular-season games last year. The Eagles have yet to pick off a pass this year, and they just got torched by Bears QB Case Keenum for 247 passing yards and two touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL MVP, Stafford returns for his 18th NFL season and his fifth with the Rams. The 38-year-old is fresh off an elite season in which he led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns, which allowed him nine top-10 fantasy weeks (tied for third most at the position). Stafford's third-place finish in fantasy points per game was his first top-10 finish since 2019, and some regression is likely due to a complete lack of rushing (65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons and one rushing touchdown since 2017). Stafford still has receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams and a strong offensive line at his disposal, so another big passing season is possible. That's just enough to keep him in the fringe QB1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mark Andrews and the Ravens host the Saints and their defense, which ranks 13th in fantasy points allowed per game (11.3) to TEs, in Week 2. Andrews caught four of his six targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 41-23 win in the season opener. He tied with Zay Flowers (hamstring) for the team lead in targets and finished second behind him in receptions. With Flowers and a host of other receivers dealing with injuries, Andrews could be in line for additional looks as a safety net for Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mark Andrews and the Ravens welcome the 0-3 Titans to town for a Week 4 showdown. After missing some time with a hand injury during Baltimore's 34-31 Week 3 win, Andrews returned and ultimately finished with three catches for 24 yards on five targets. He's still in search of his first TD of 2026, but he's been consistently involved on offense, totaling 18 targets across three contests. Andrews could find it difficult to break through in the scoring department against the Titans' third-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (7.4) to TEs, as they're one of nine teams yet to surrender a receiving touchdown to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: One of fantasy's biggest mysteries, Andrews' usage has dipped substantially over the past two seasons. After finishing in the top five in fantasy PPG five seasons in a row from 2019 to 2023, Andrews slipped to eighth in 2024 (it would've been much worse if not for 11 touchdowns on 68 targets) and fell even further to 24th last season. Andrews appeared in all 17 of Baltimore's games but ranked 18th among tight ends in targets and outside the top 20 in catches and yards. The combination of a new coaching staff, a healthy Lamar Jackson and the departure of Isaiah Likely could lead to a rebound season for Andrews, but we now have two straight seasons of underperformance. The 31-year-old remains a force near the goal line (top 10 in end zone targets seven years in a row), but he's now more of a fringe TE1 than a fantasy star.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deebo Samuel will look to build upon a strong season-opening performance when the 49ers face Miami in Week 2. In Samuel's return to San Francisco following a one-year hiatus, he caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in last Thursday's win over the Rams. Samuel and Mike Evans finished with nearly identical receiving lines, suggesting that both veteran wideouts can thrive with QB Brock Purdy. The Dolphins were beat handily by the Raiders in Week 1 while giving up three TDs through the air (though two were to RB Ashton Jeanty).
outlooksByWeek.3: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Deebo Samuel could take on the 49ers' No. 1 WR role in Week 4 against Denver if Mike Evans (ribs/oblique) is unable to play. Though Evans left in the second quarter in this past Sunday's win over Arizona, Samuel ended the contest without seeing a target. However, he still had a good fantasy line thanks to an 80-yard TD on a hook-and-ladder play, and Samuel also gained 14 yards on two carries. Should Evans be unable to suit up against Denver, Samuel could face the daunting task of trying to beat star cornerback Patrick Surtain.

player.seasonOutlook: Samuel reunited with the 49ers in July after solid yet unspectacular lone season in Washington. The former second-round pick cleared 85 touches and 800 scrimmage yards for the fifth consecutive season and finished 25th among receivers in fantasy points -- his third-career top-30 fantasy campaign. Samuel's role as a short-area target and occasional rusher gets the ball in his hands plenty (he's ranked in the top 15 among WRs in touches and RAC five years in a row), but it doesn't allow him much scoring upside (10 TDs over the last two years, and he's never cleared five end zone targets in one season). Now 30 years old, Samuel figures to resume his role as a short-area playmaker in Kyle Shanahan's highly-efficient offense. He's a fine late-round flier with WR3/flex upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Romeo Doubs will seek a larger role in the Patriots' passing game in Week 2 against the Steelers. Doubs failed to record a catch on three targets in his team debut, playing only 56% of the snaps despite New England losing A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain. With Brown set to miss significant time, Doubs should garner more opportunities, but it looks as though he's still developing chemistry with Drake Maye. Questions remain regarding the Steelers' secondary, which is likely to remain without Joey Porter Jr. They weren't tested last week, but counting on a breakthrough from Doubs is risky.
outlooksByWeek.3: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.
outlooksByWeek.4: Romeo Doubs' workload remains minimal for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Despite A.J. Brown's absence (ankle), Doubs has just 11 targets through three weeks. He's averaging a robust 24.2 yards per reception, and the Bills are allowing a big 9.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts. With Drake Maye struggling, gambling on a few Week 4 chunk plays is risky.

player.seasonOutlook: Doubs signed with the Patriots during free agency after spending his first four NFL seasons with the Packers. He was a serviceable player during his Green Bay tenure, but he never finished a season in the top 30 among receivers in targets, catches, yards or fantasy points. Consistently mediocre, Doubs has averaged either 10.2 or 10.3 fantasy PPG each of the last three seasons. In New England, Doubs is likely to settle in as Drake Maye's No. 2 target behind A.J. Brown, though his target ceiling figures to be capped with the likes of DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams also in the mix at receiver. Doubs, 26, is a fine addition to your bench, but his upside is limited.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt found the end zone in Week 1 for Washington.  Bill served as the primary ballcarrier, toting the pigskin 16 times for 63 yards and the score. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White had seven carries for only 22 years. In Week 2, Croskey-Merritt will have a favorable matchup versus the Cowboys. Dallas allowed 165 yards rushing and one score on the ground to the Giants in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jacory Croskey-Merritt was perhaps predictably stymied by the Seattle Seahawks last game. However, the touches were a silver lining, as Croskey-Merritt garnered 20 opportunities in the 33-31 win over the defending champions. Bill rushed 19 times for 36 yards, while also catching a seven-yard pass out of the backfield. However, fellow running back Rachaad White  averaged more than double Croskey-Meritt's yards per carry, while also finding the end zone through the air. However, there could be plenty of room to roam in Week 4 versus the Colts. Indianapolis has been dreadful against the run in 2026, allowing 141.3 yards per contest on he ground, which is 29th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: One of the most hyped-up players entering the 2025 fantasy season, Croskey-Merritt didn't quite live up to lofty expectations, but he was certainly very busy for a seventh-round rookie. "Bill" played 39% of Washington's offensive snaps but, while he finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards, he wasn't much of a factor in the passing game (3% target share). Croskey-Merritt will now compete with newcomer Rachaad White in what appears to be setting up as a committee in Washington. The 25-year-old has shown to be an effective rusher (4.60 yards per carry, 2.19 YAC), but he'll need a big boost in receiving work to find his way into the RB2/flex discussion. He's worth only a late-round flier.

This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashee Rice took advantage of his limited volume in Kansas City's season-opening win over the Broncos, catching both his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown. Patrick Mahomes didn't have to throw much, as Kenneth Walker had a career-best day on the ground and the team had a comfortable lead in the second half. Better performances should be ahead for Rice in more favorable game scripts, but returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy could also be planning to lean on his running game more heavily than in years past. Rice will look to follow in Zay Flowers' footsteps in Week 2 against a Colts secondary that ranked 30th in points per game allowed to WRs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashee Rice hasn't yet put together a breakout game for Kansas City in 2026. The fourth-year wide receiver has a solid 13-190-1 line on 17 targets through three weeks, but Patrick Mahomes hasn't focused on any one pass catcher and has been spreading the ball around effectively. Rice, Travis Kelce, Xavier Worthy, and Kenneth Walker all have between 15 and 18 targets. Rice could have a hard time improving on his numbers in Week 4 against a Raiders secondary that ranks second in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Rice enters Year 4 of his career still seeking his first full season as a starter. The 2023 second-round pick was sidelined for most of 2024 due to injury and missed nine games last season due to suspension (Weeks 1-6) and injury (Weeks 16-18). The good news is that Rice remained highly productive when active. He handled 9.8 targets per game and was a top-12 fantasy receiver in five of his eight outings in 2025. Rice is Patrick Mahomes' top target, and his 8.0 RAC is tops among qualified receivers over the past three seasons. With Mahomes (ACL recovery) ready to go in Week 1 as expected, Rice finds himself in the WR1 mix.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trevor Lawrence threw four touchdown passes in the first 33 minutes of Jacksonville's lopsided Week 1 win over the Browns before the Jaguars took their foot off the gas. He has 22 touchdown passes in his last eight starts, but the surging QB could face a stiffer test in a Week 2 road game against the Broncos. They boasted the NFL's third-stingiest scoring defense last season but just gave up 31 points to the Chiefs in Week 1. Lawrence has been effective enough recently to warrant starting in fantasy despite the daunting matchup, but he's unlikely to give managers a top-five performance in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least three touchdown passes in two of three games this season but is averaging just 205 passing yards per game. He'll maintain an elite ceiling in Jacksonville's Week 4 road game against the Bengals, who have allowed the third-most passing yards. Cincinnati just gave up three passing TDs to Aaron Rodgers in Week 3 but hadn't allowed a touchdown pass prior to that game this season. Lawrence has been a fantasy QB1 more often than not since Parker Washington emerged as his go-to receiver in the second half of last season, and that looks unlikely to change in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Lawrence is entering his sixth NFL season after a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in pass attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns, as well as top 10 in carries, yards and TDs. He reeled off seven consecutive top-10 fantasy outings to finish the season. Lawrence's efficiency has been fine, at best, but he continues to generate big volume, having finished in the top 10 among QBs in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. With a strong, deep group of pass catchers and Liam Coen back as playcaller, the 26-year-old is well positioned for mid-to-back-end QB1 production.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Darren Waller continues to emerge as a major part of the Panthers' passing attack ahead of the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Waller had his most productive outing of the 2026 campaign in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, catching five of eight targets for 51 yards. He's taken over as Carolina's top receiving option at TE and could continue receiving more opportunities if Jalen Coker (hamstring) or Xavier Legette (knee) remain sidelined for Week 4. Regardless, Waller is in for a phenomenal Week 4 matchup against a Detroit defense that's allowed a whopping six receiving touchdowns to tight ends in three games this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kalif Raymond could continue to be a consistent option as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Raymond benefited from a high-scoring Week 1 win, reeling in eight of nine targets for 84 yards. The veteran wide receiver was also on the field for 60 percent of offensive snaps, so it appears at least a WR3 role is cemented moving forward. He'll face a Minnesota defense that ceded the second-most PPR points (55.2) to his position this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kalif Raymond will look to stay involved as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Raymond was a consistent option once again in Week 2 against the Vikings, catching all five of his targets for 40 yards. The veteran wide receiver has now recorded 13 catches for 124 yards on 14 targets through two games. With quarterback Tyson Bagent also slated to get the start under center, Raymond could be a safe target against a middle-of-the-pack Philly defense against WRs (29.4 PPR points per game).
outlooksByWeek.4: Kalif Raymond will look to continue his tear as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Raymond remained a top option in Chicago's passing game in Week 3 against the Eagles, pulling in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown. The Lion transfer has now garnered five or more targets in each game this season, and eclipsed 80 yards in two of three. He'll face a Jets secondary that's been tougher on WRs this season, allowing a top-five 337 receiving yards to the position so far.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Carlson will look to remain productive in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Carlson converted his first four kicks (two field goals and two extra points) before missing a 62-yard field-goal attempt on the last play of regulation. He's expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities moving forward but may struggle against the Ravens in Week 2, as they allowed just 5.0 kicking points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Carlson is expected to have few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Carlson, who spent the previous eight seasons with the Raiders, converted on all three of his field-goal tries during the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He could continue to receive scoring opportunities due to New Orleans' offensive success. However, Carlson is likely in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, as Las Vegas has allowed just 4.5 kicking points per game this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Daniel Carlson could see few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. Carlson has been relatively accurate in his first three games with New Orleans, converting on seven of eight extra-point attempts and four of five field-goal tries. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high-powered offense, which is currently averaging 27.0 points per game. However, Carlson is in for a tough Week 4 matchup, as the Falcons' defense has allowed just 6.7 kicking points per game this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals take on the Texans, who ranked 26th in fantasy points allowed per game (41.5) to WRs in Week 2. After a two-catch, 12-yard dud in the season opener, he'll be aiming for a big bounce-back performance against a vulnerable secondary. Chase logged just four targets in Week 1 despite 35 pass attempts from Joe Burrow. The QB-WR duo should be primed for a rebound against a Houston defense that gave up 409 total yards at home last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He caught nine of 12 targets for 98 yards and his third receiving touchdown of the season during Cincinnati's Week 3 defeat. Chase led the team in receptions, yardage, and targets, and it's clear that his two-catch, 12-yard outing in the season opener was a fluke. He should continue garnering a massive target share from star QB Joe Burrow against Jacksonville's 17th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (31.5) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Chase is fresh off yet another elite fantasy season and he's now finished four of his five NFL campaigns no lower than fifth in fantasy PPG (the exception was 11th in 2023). Chase actually saw a big dip in yardage (1,740 to 1,426), TDs (17 to 8) and fantasy PPG (23.7 to 19.6) from 2024 to 2025 (which was no surprise with Joe Burrow missing nine games), but still put up big numbers thanks to pacing the league in pass routes and targets for the second season in a row. In fact, Chase's 125 receptions make him the third receiver in NFL history with 125-plus catches in multiple seasons. The 26-year-old remains the top target in a high-scoring Bengals offense, and is one of the top players in all of fantasy.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeVonta Smith was fairly quiet in the season opener for the Eagles. Smith finished with three catches for 53 yards in the 24-22 win over Washington. On the plus side, Smith led the team in targets for the game with six. The absence of A. J. Brown should pay dividends for Smith, perhaps as early as Week 2 versus the Titans. Tennessee allowed 215 passing yards and zero touchdowns through the air in its season opener, though the opposing quarterback was Geno Smith of the New York Jets. Expect Smith to become more involved against a suspect defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.
outlooksByWeek.4: DeVonta Smith unsurprisingly led the Eagles in targets, receptions and receiving yardage last game. Unfortunately, the output was rather pedestrian, as Smith managed six catches and 65 yards on eight targets in the ugly 27-7 loss to the Bears. Smith has been held under 70 yards receiving in two of his three games this season. In Week 4, he will face a rather stingy Rams pass defense allowing just 171.3 yards per game through the air, which is fourth in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: It's generally tough for a former Heisman Trophy winner and first-round draft pick to fly under the radar, but that has been the case for Smith in recent years. With all eyes on A.J. Brown, Smith has finished no lower than 30th among receivers in fantasy PPG in each of his five seasons (top 30 in PPG each of the last four). The "slim reaper" saw a big dip in touchdowns last season (four, after at least seven the prior three seasons), but remained very efficient (career 9.1 yards per target and 2.1 yards per route run). Smith has handled roughly one-quarter of the Eagles' targets throughout his career, and that may rise slightly after Brown was traded to New England. Smith, 27, is the Eagles' No. 1 receiver for the first time as a non-rookie and is well positioned for a strong WR2 campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Saints to town for a Week 2 matchup. Flowers left Baltimore's 41-23 Week 1 win in the second quarter and did not return. He is considered day-to-day with a hamstring injury, per head coach Jesse Minter. Soft tissue injuries can be tricky, especially for someone as shifty as Flowers, but it sounds like the issue is not considered serious. He's fresh off posting a career-high 150 receiving yards on five catches (six targets) and a TD, so if the speedster is active against New Orleans, he should see plenty of looks from Lamar Jackson.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zay Flowers and the Ravens welcome the Titans to town in Week 4. He returned from a one-game absence in Week 2 due to a hamstring injury and handled a full workload, catching five of six targets for 84 yards while taking his lone carry for 20 yards during Baltimore's Week 3 victory. Flowers led the team in receptions, targets, and yardage, and that should remain the same against Tennessee, which has the 18th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (32.9) to WRs. The hamstring issue appears to be behind him for now, but managers will want to keep an eye on his practice reps leading up to Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Flowers' emergence into a star continued in 2025, as the 2023 first-round pick posted career-best marks in target share (29%), targets (118), catches (86) and yardage (1,211). Despite still lacking a role near the goal line (he has never cleared seven end zone targets or six touchdowns in a single season), Flowers finished seventh among receivers in fantasy points (13th PPG), which marks his first finish better than 25th (31st PPG). A highly targeted, short-range RAC specialist, Flowers' ceiling is lower than other top receivers, but the 25-year-old remains positioned as Lamar Jackson's top target in Baltimore's new-look offense. Flowers makes for a solid fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the Saints for an interconference showdown in Week 2. Jackson was stellar in the opener despite losing a fumble, throwing for 324 yards (17-for-25) with one TD and no picks while rushing seven times for another 40 yards and a TD. Although he still offers elite upside at the QB position, it's important to note that his favorite receiver, Zay Flowers, is dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Jesse Minter considers "day-to-day." The two connected on five of six targets for 150 yards and a score in the victory. The New Orleans defense ranks 12th in fantasy points allowed per game (18.5) to QBs after Jared Goff's 206 yards and two TDs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens host the 0-3 Titans for a Week 4 showdown. In Baltimore's thrilling 34-31 win over Dallas in Week 3, he connected on 15 of 20 throws for 186 yards with two TDs and no INTs while rushing six times for 50 yards, including a 27-yard strike to Zay Flowers that helped set up the game-winning field goal as time expired. Tennessee's defense has been stingy, allowing just 13.9 fantasy points per game to QBs through three games, which ranks first. Jackson should have his full complement of receivers available as the Ravens aim to improve to 3-1 on the season.

player.seasonOutlook: Jackson, 29, is eyeing a rebound after a disappointing, injury-plagued 2025. Jackson started the season strong (26-plus fantasy points in each of his first three games) but left Week 4 because of an injury and wasn't the same once he returned in Week 9 (13.5 fantasy points per game in his final nine outings). Jackson's overall rushing was down, but that was likely a product of him not being fully healthy, especially considering his scramble rate (8.4%) remained high. Jackson has a new coach (Jesse Minter) and playcaller (Declan Doyle), but his supporting cast is otherwise similar to a 2024 campaign in which he paced all quarterbacks in fantasy points. Assuming he's back to full health, Jackson is a strong bet for a rebound and should be valued as a high-end QB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tony Pollard got just eight touches in the season opener as the Titans fell behind against the Jets and abandoned the run. Negative game scripts could be a recurring problem for Pollard, and the Titans will be substantial Week 2 underdogs at home against the Eagles. On the bright side, Pollard recorded at least 1,288 scrimmage yards in each of the previous two seasons, even as the Titans posted a 3-14 record both years. Pollard's status as the team's starting running back keeps him in the Week 2 flex/RB3 conversation.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).
outlooksByWeek.4: Tony Pollard has increased his yardage total in each of Tennessee's first three games heading into a Week 4 road game against the Ravens, who are allowing 99 scrimmage yards per game to RBs. Pollard had just 34 scrimmage yards on eight touches in a lopsided Week 1 loss to the Jets, but he recorded 65 yards on 15 touches in Week 2 and 96 scrimmage yards on 21 touches in Week 3 as the Titans managed to stay within striking distance before falling to the Eagles and Giants, respectively. With second-year QB Cam Ward struggling to move the ball through the air, the Titans will likely try to continue featuring their Pollard-led ground game, though there is a substantial risk of Lamar Jackson and the Ravens pulling away and forcing Tennessee into a more pass-heavy game plan. Given Pollard's status as the lead back in a low-octane offense, he has a decent floor as a flex play but isn't the most exciting Week 4 RB option.

player.seasonOutlook: Pollard has handled a hefty 67.2% of the Titans' designed rushing attempts since his arrival two seasons ago (15.2 per game) and, even with solid efficiency, he has finished 22nd and 30th in fantasy points per game. The culprits? Tennessee's struggling offense (Pollard has exactly five TDs in both seasons) and a limited receiving role when Tyjae Spears has been healthy (Pollard's targets fell from 3.5 per game in 2024 to 2.5 per game in 2025). Barring a major leap from quarterback Cam Ward, Pollard is unlikely to deliver only the second top-20 fantasy campaign (in points per game) of his career. The 29-year-old, entering his eighth NFL season (third with Tennessee), is a low-ceiling flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots. He rushed eight times for 15 yards and caught two of five targets for another six yards during Pittsburgh's Week 1 20-13 win over Atlanta. Dowdle's backfield partner, Jaylen Warren, was much more efficient with his 15 touches, which he turned into 73 scrimmage yards. It will be difficult to trust Dowdle in a tilt versus New England's 14th-ranked defense, which has allowed 84 rushing yards to the position.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers visit the division-rival Browns for a Week 4 road tilt. He sat out Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory with a toe injury he sustained in Week 2, and it looks like he's in real jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest. Dowdle didn't practice at all last week and was not present at Monday's walkthrough session, which isn't a great sign for his availability on a short week. He'll have to practice in some capacity if he hopes to face Cleveland's sixth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.1) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dowdle signed with the Steelers after nearly identical campaigns with the Cowboys in 2024 (1,328 yards and five TDs on 274 touches) and Panthers in 2025 (1,373 yards and seven TDs on 275 touches). He was effective as a rusher (4.57 yards per carry) and fairly busy as a receiver (50 targets both years) en route to finishing just inside the top 25 in fantasy points per game both seasons. Now in Pittsburgh, the 28-year-old is expected to share work with Jaylen Warren. Earning lead-rusher duties could get Dowdle into the weekly flex discussion, but the ceiling will be low and he'll likely need an injury in order to find his way to consistent fantasy output. Consider him for your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Downs is hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league flex for the Colts' Week 2 trip to Kansas City. His four targets in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore tied for fourth on the team with Jonathan Taylor, as Daniel Jones threw more frequently to Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Tyler Warren. In 17 appearances since the start of last season, Downs is averaging a pedestrian 35.5 receiving yards per game in the Colts' run-heavy offense.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Downs has exceeded 70 receiving yards in each of the Colts' last two games while racking up 20 targets over that span. With fellow Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) on IR, Downs is a recommended Week 4 starting option since he is poised to see plenty of targets from Daniel Jones against a weak Washington secondary that has allowed the most catches (46) and touchdown receptions (six) to WRs, as well as the third-most receiving yards (573) to the position. Downs, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Keenan Allen accounted for 20 of Jones' 24 completed passes in Pierce's absence against the Texans in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Downs has settled in as a serviceable slot receiver, which has helped him to finish in the 35-to-45 range among WRs in total fantasy points in each of his three NFL seasons. Downs peaked with a 72-803-5 receiving line in 2024, but took a step back in a crowded offense last season, and failed to deliver a single fantasy week better than 15th at the position. The undersized Downs isn't an option near the goal line, as he hasn't cleared five touchdowns or three end zone targets in a single season. The 25-year-old has a path to a slightly larger role in 2026 with Michael Pittman Jr. gone, leaving Alec Pierce, Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen as his primary target competition. Downs is a sleeper for flex production in PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dalton Kincaid will look to match a career outing when the Bills face the Lions in Week 2. Kincaid had a personal-best 130 yards in his season debut but, more importantly, played 77% of the team's snaps after topping 50% just three times last year. If Kincaid remains on the field at this rate, he's likely to soar past his previous season's output. He'll face a defense on Thursday night that allowed 87 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends in Week 1, suggesting his statistical surge can continue.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.
outlooksByWeek.4: Dalton Kincaid will seek to rebuild momentum when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. After gaining 225 yards in Weeks 1 and 2, Kincaid had just two catches for 38 yards in Week 3. Part of the decrease in volume could be DJ Moore's return to health, but Buffalo remains run-heavy, limiting Kincaid's looks. He recorded a 67% snap share, more than usual, so opportunity remains. Facing a Patriots defense that has defended the tight end position well dampens hope, having allowed only 84 total yards to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: Kincaid is perhaps fantasy's biggest wild card among tight ends. The 2023 first-round pick has occasionally flashed a high ceiling (he actually led qualified tight ends in YPT and YPRR last season), but he also has missed substantial action (nine games the past two years) and has disappeared way too often (he failed to clear 13.1 fantasy points in any game in 2024, and never cleared six targets in a game in 2025). Kincaid was limited to a 37% snap share when active last season, and he has yet to finish a season better than 14th in fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old has TE1 upside, but he's tough to trust and has added target competition (WR DJ Moore) in 2026. Consider Kincaid only in the mid-to-late rounds.

Charbonnet would've been entering his fourth NFL season as the clear lead back in Seattle, but a torn ACL during the team's playoff game against the 49ers has put his 2026 campaign in jeopardy. It's a tough break for the 2020 second-round NFL draft pick, who set career-high marks in touches (204) while ranking fifth among backs in rushing touchdowns (12) and carries inside the 5-yard line (16) last season. Charbonnet's minimal receiving role (career-low 24 targets) limited him to 11.3 fantasy points per game, however, and he has yet to deliver a top-20 fantasy campaign. Kenneth Walker III is gone, but first-round rookie Jadarian Price could very well cement himself a big offensive role by the time Charbonnet is healthy. The 25-year-old is worth only a late-round lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kyren Williams may again be part of a pretty evenly split backfield when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Though Williams scored Los Angeles' only touchdown in a season-opening loss to the 49ers, he had 13 fewer rushing yards on one more carry than backfield mate Blake Corum. Williams did produce more total yards thanks to logging 24 receiving yards on three catches, but Corum seems to have forced his way into a substantial backfield role after averaging over five yards per carry last year. Both backs will look to break through a Giants defense that gave up just 69 yards and 3.8 YPC against Dallas in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kyren Williams is fresh off his most productive performance of the campaign heading into the Rams' Week 4 clash against Philadelphia. Williams posted season-best tallies with 15 carries for 88 yards in Week 3 against Denver, and he complemented his output on the ground with a season-high six catches for 70 yards through the air. Whereas fellow running back Blake Corum has frequently eaten into Williams' volume since last season, Corum recorded just six totes and 15 total yards against the Broncos. Corum isn't likely to exit the picture anytime soon, but Williams remains a consistent week-to-week producer. However, he could have his work cut out for him in Week 4 versus an Eagles defense that ranks 12th in the league in fantasy points allowed to running backs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams continues to produce at a high level as the Rams' lead back. The 2022 fifth-round pick has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons (including a career-high 1,533 in 2025), and he's one of 11 backs in NFL history who have scored 13-plus touchdowns in three of his first four seasons. Williams' carry share actually dropped quite a bit last season, but it was mostly offset by a boost in both rushing and receiving efficiency, and he still averaged a healthy 15.5 fantasy points. Williams doesn't do much as a receiver (he has never cleared 36 catches in a season), but his overall usage and scoring potential in the Rams' elite offense is enough to make the 26-year-old a solid RB2 option.

Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kenyon Sadiq could have an emerging role for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Sadiq notched four touches in his NFL debut, including a three-yard rushing score, out-gaining starter Mason Taylor handsomely in a run-heavy game for the Jets. They'll likely need to throw more to keep up with Green Bay's offense in Week 2, and the Packers allowed a touchdown to a tight end last week. The floor is volatile, but Sadiq offers high ceiling potential for those in need at tight end.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kenyon Sadiq could be poised for a major breakout for the Jets in Week 3 if Mason Taylor (thumb) is unable to play against the Lions. Sadiq has played just 42% and 38% of the offensive snaps through two games, easing into the rotation after recovering from hernia surgery prior to the year. The Jets' offense isn't prolific, but the matchup with a porous Lions' defense could change that. Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to opposing tight ends in each of the first two weeks and 187 total yards, the second-highest total across the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Kenyon Sadiq could struggle to build on a breakout performance in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. After recording just six targets in his first two games, Sadiq shined in Week 3, catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a touchdown, despite playing just 56% of the offensive snaps in Mason Taylor's absence. The Bears have not allowed an opposing tight end to top 30 yards this season, with teams finding more success targeting their corners, so a repeat performance may be challenging.

player.seasonOutlook: Sadiq was selected by the Jets with the No. 16 pick of April's draft. After playing a limited role his first two collegiate seasons, he broke out with a 51-560-8 receiving line in 2025. He handled a respectable 17% of Oregon's targets and aligned in the slot 62% of the time. Sadiq is a bit on the small side, but he totaled 106 targets in three collegiate seasons. He needs to cut down on drops (six on 70 targets in 2025), but he's one of the youngest players in this rookie class and crushed it at the combine, posting a ridiculous 4.39 40-yard dash at 241 pounds (130 speed score) and a 43.5-inch vertical, 133-inch broad jump and 26 bench reps. Sadiq's career might start slow, especially with Mason Taylor also on the Jets' TE depth chart, but the rookie has the upside to eventually emerge as a fantasy TE1. Consider him with a mid-to-late pick.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving room during the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 9.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the NFL. Despite not receiving a target in his NFL debut, Branch tied Olamide Zaccheaus for the third-most snaps (18) amongst Falcons receivers. Additionally, he could be more involved in the Week 2 gameplan after Atlanta's offensive struggles last week. Even so, Branch is in for a great matchup against a Panthers defense that gave up eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.
outlooksByWeek.4: Zachariah Branch is expected to remain a minimal portion of the Falcons' offensive game plan in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints, Through three weeks, Branch has caught three of four targets while playing 45 offensive snaps. Despite not having much competition in Atlanta's WR room, the rookie wideout likely won't have fantasy value without finding the end zone in Week 4. Additionally, Branch could struggle against a good New Orleans secondary that's allowed just 6.2 yards per pass attempt this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary competition. Branch should only be drafted in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain an important part of the Saints' offense in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Vele saw nine targets in the Week 1 overtime loss, tying his career high and trailing only Chris Olave in the Saints' receiving corps. Vele should continue to benefit from the absence of Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and is expected to see consistent volume until Tyson returns. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup for Vele, however, as the Ravens' defense has given up just 4.8 yards per pass attempt this season, which is tied for the second-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Devaughn Vele is likely to remain the Saints' second option at wideout in the Week 4 matchup against the Falcons. While Jordan Tyson (hamstring) has been sidelined, Vele has been very fantasy-relevant, catching 15 of 22 targets for 172 yards and a touchdown (12.7 PPR points per game). Vele has almost no competition outside of Chris Olave in the Saints' WR room, which bodes well for his fantasy outlook going forward. Additionally, New Orleans' offense is averaging 44 pass attempts per game, which suggests Vele will continue having scoring opportunities. He's in for a favorable Week 4 matchup, as Atlanta's defense has allowed 604 receiving yards to wideouts this season, the most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be relied on for consistent targets and fantasy production, but he'll play an every-down role early on, which makes him a sleeper for flex value in deep leagues. He'll be worth a roster spot until Tyson returns.

outlooksByWeek.2: Spencer Shrader made a 58-yard field goal but also missed an extra point in a confounding performance during the Colts' season-opening loss. The big-legged kicker may not get many opportunities in Week 2 against the Chiefs, especially since the Colts are one of the league's most efficient red-zone teams thanks to the presence of star RB Jonathan Taylor. Shrader is a middling fantasy option, and you can likely find a kicker in a more appealing situation on your league's waiver wire.
outlooksByWeek.3: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.
outlooksByWeek.4: Spencer Shrader is coming off a heroic performance in the Colts' 19-17 Week 3 win over the Texans, as the kicker overcame an early groin injury to make all four of his field-goal attempts, including a go-ahead 53-yarder with 16 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He's off to an 8-for-8 start this season and has made kicks from as deep as 58 yards. Shrader is making a case for a starting fantasy kicker role, and he'll have a chance to showcase his skills on the international stage in Week 4, when the Colts face the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Scoring opportunities are likely to be plentiful for Shrader since Washington is giving up 30.7 points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers hope to improve to 2-0 when they visit the Patriots in Week 2. He secured all five targets for 46 yards and Aaron Rodgers' lone passing TD, and finished second on the team in receiving yards while tying for first in receptions. Freiermuth led Pittsburgh's TEs in offensive snaps (49), but Darnell Washington was a close second with 43. He and the Steelers will try to scheme up a way to beat a New England defense that is tied for second in receiving yards allowed to the position (13).
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.
outlooksByWeek.4: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 4 AFC North clash against the Browns. He caught two of four targets for 30 yards and rushed once for one yard during Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory. Aaron Rodgers continues to spread the ball around, as six different Steelers receivers registered at least four targets, and four tied for the team lead in receptions with three. Freiermuth could be a sneaky play versus a Cleveland defense that ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (14.9) to TEs and gave up eight receptions (on 12 targets) for 92 yards to the position in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Freiermuth's career trajectory has been quite the head-scratcher, but the bottom line is he is yet to emerge as a consistent fantasy starter. The 2021 second-round pick flirted with TE1 status in both 2022 (11th in fantasy PPG) and 2024 (14th) but saw a dramatic dip in usage in Pittsburgh's crowded tight end room in 2025. Freiermuth posted a career-low 10% target share and finished outside the top 20 at the position in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards and end zone targets, and 30 tight ends bested his 6.7 fantasy PPG. The 27-year-old figures to play more in 2026 with Jonnu Smith gone and Mike McCarthy running the offense, but Pittsburgh is also better at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard in the fold. Freiermuth has some sleeper appeal, but he's best valued as a back-end TE2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Coker (ankle) will look to continue shining in Carolina's Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Coker has shown out in the Panthers last two games (including their wild-card loss to end last season), having recorded a combined 17 receptions for 272 yards and three touchdowns. He's outproduced 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan and looks to be a major part of Carolina's offense going forward. However, Coker is dealing with an ankle issue and could struggle against a tough Falcons defense that gave up just 5.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is expected to operate as one of the Panthers' top targets if active for the Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Coker has dealt with three separate injuries through three weeks this season (ankle, hamstring and quadriceps). Despite this, the third-year wideout has amassed 222 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 18 catches, leading the Panthers in yards and touchdowns. If Coker is able to suit up in Week 4, he's in for an incredibly favorable matchup, as Detroit's defense has allowed a whopping 31.7 points and 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to the WR position this season.

player.seasonOutlook: After missing nearly the entire first half of 2025, Coker passed Xavier Legette and took on a larger offensive role opposite Tetairoa McMillan. From Week 8 onward (11 games, including the playoffs), Coker played 73% of the snaps and handled a 17.8% target share. The fantasy output was inconsistent (below 11.5 points in seven games), but he peaked down the stretch (more than 14 points in four of his final six, including a 9-134-1 showing against the Rams in the playoffs). Coker's strong finish is encouraging, though his rookie season went similarly (14-plus points three times, but under 11 in the other nine games). A healthy 2026 could get Coker to the next level, but flex production is his likely ceiling as long as McMillan is commanding one-quarter (if not more) of the targets in Carolina's Bryce Young-led offense.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

outlooksByWeek.2: Raheim Sanders and the Browns are on the road to square off against the Buccaneers in Week 2. After Dylan Sampson (knee) was ruled out in the first half, Sanders filled in as the No. 2 RB behind Quinshon Judkins. He notched one carry for one yard and caught all three targets for 25 yards while playing 16 snaps on offense. With Cleveland expected to play from behind often, Sanders could have a fairly sizable role in the passing game, no matter who the quarterback is. Tampa Bay allowed eight catches on nine targets for 52 yards to RBs in their Week 1 loss.
outlooksByWeek.3: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3. He tallied two carries for four yards and caught his only target for seven yards during Cleveland's first win of the season in Week 2. Quinshon Judkins handled 12 of 15 carries by running backs, and as long as he remains healthy, the workload split should remain similar. Sanders does have some upside as a receiver out of the backfield, but his role is still too limited to be relied upon in fantasy. Carolina's defense has been susceptible on the ground, allowing 36.3 fantasy points to RBs (31st), but they rank 14th in receiving yards surrendered to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the rival Steelers for a divisional clash in Week 4. He took his lone carry for 17 yards and caught four of five targets for 34 yards during Cleveland's upset win in Week 3. Sanders was highly efficient with his five touches, finishing second on the team in receptions and third in targets. He should continue operating as the third-down back and in most passing situations, but his overall involvement is difficult to trust while Quinshon Judkins remains healthy. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points (22.1) and 25th in receiving yards allowed to RBs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian McCaffrey is coming off his best game of the campaign heading into San Francisco's Week 4 tilt versus the Broncos. McCaffrey compiled season-high marks with 75 rushing yards and 116 total yards in Sunday's win against Arizona while scoring his third TD of 2026. His 15 carries were also his most so far this season, as the 49ers appear to be pulling back on his workload a bit after he led the NFL with 413 touches last year. McCaffrey could find room to run on Denver, as the Broncos have so far given up the second-most rushing yards to RBs (129.7 per game) this season.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

outlooksByWeek.2: CeeDee Lamb found the end zone for the Cowboys while leading the squad in receiving in Week 1. However, Lamb finished with five catches for just 44 yards in the dismal 28-20 loss to the Giants. Still, Lamb led the team in targets, and the touchdown salvaged his day from a fantasy perspective. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game.
