He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: CeeDee Lamb crossed the 100-yard mark for the second-straight week for the Cowboys. Lamb snagged seven balls for 112 yards in the 34-31 loss to the Ravens. Unfortunately, Lamb was held out of the end zone for the first time all season. However, Lamb has at least eight targets in each of the first three games for Dallas, and should stay in busy in Week 4 versus the Texans, even if he is guarded by all-pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. The Cowboys will face a Texans defense that has been surprisingly suspect against the pass in 2026.  Houston is allowing 238.7 passing yards per tilt, which is 25th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Lamb is eyeing a bounceback season following a 2025 campaign in which he finished 12th among receivers in fantasy PPG � his worst finish since 2021. Lamb did go over 1,000 yards for the fifth season in a row, but he missed three games, led all receivers with eight drops and was unlucky in the TD department, having scored three touchdowns (6.6 expected) despite seeing 11 end zone targets. Lamb, 27, remains in his prime and he was fantasy's top-scoring receiver the last time he played a full season (2023). As long Dak Prescott is on the field with him, Lamb will be a solid fantasy WR1 with elite upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Allen appears to have the Bills' offense humming as they get set to host the Lions in Week 2. Facing a stout Texans defense last week, Allen accounted for 357 total yards and four touchdowns, against a unit he had previously struggled. No such fears should exist Thursday night, as the Lions' depleted secondary is coming off a game where they allowed 410 yards and three touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.
outlooksByWeek.4: Josh Allen will look for a bounce-back performance when the Bills face the Patriots in Week 4. Allen failed to throw a touchdown pass in Week 3 for the first time this season, while also tossing his first two interceptions. He rushed for two scores for the third straight week and has at least six carries in three straight games, but he's completed 20 passes or fewer in every outing. He'll oppose a familiar opponent in a Patriots defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks despite yielding three touchdown passes by Trevor Lawrence in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Allen enters his age-30 campaign having finished each of the past six seasons no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points. Despite seeing less passing volume the past two seasons (14th or lower in pass attempts both years), the 2024 NFL MVP has finished in the top 10 in passing TDs six seasons in a row and remains a major threat with his legs (top five in carries and rushing TDs among quarterbacks all eight seasons of his career). Allen's 21.4 fantasy points per game in 2025 was actually his lowest since 2019, but it was still enough to lead the position. With Joe Brady returning as playcaller and the Bills adding a No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, Allen remains an elite fantasy quarterback.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to operate as Carolina's top pass catcher in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. McMillan caught just five passes for 75 yards and lost a fumble in last week's loss, despite the game ending with the most points ever scored in a Week 1 contest. He was out-shined by third-year wideout Jalen Coker, who paced Carolina's receiving corps in targets (nine), receptions (eight), yards (138) and touchdowns (two). McMillan will look to return to form in Week 2, but he's in for a tough matchup against a Falcons defense that gave up just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.
outlooksByWeek.4: Tetairoa McMillan will look to bounce back from an underwhelming performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year was held to just two catches for 17 yards in the Week 3 loss to the Browns, the second-fewest yards he's ever recorded in an NFL game. Despite this, McMillan has an extremely positive outlook going forward, as both Jalen Coker (quadriceps) and Xavier Legette (knee) are dealing with injuries, making him the clear number one target. Additionally, McMillan is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Lions defense that's allowed 39.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: The reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, McMillan is a candidate to make the leap into the "elite" conversation at wide receiver this season. The 2025 eighth overall pick was very busy as a rookie (top 15 among WRs in snaps, routes, target share, targets, yards, end zone targets and touchdowns) and, while he finished 16th among receivers in fantasy points (22nd PPG), he lacked upside, producing only one top-10 outing (Week 9). Improving on a 56% catch rate will be key in Year 2, though that would require improvement from Bryce Young. McMillan, 23, remains positioned as Carolina's clear top target and, though Young's limitations may cap his ceiling a bit, McMillan's talent/usage combo supplies him with top-10 upside. He's safest as a midrange fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Courtland Sutton was held in check along with the rest of the Broncos' offense in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching two of five targets for just 11 yards. Quarterback Bo Nix couldn't connect with either of his top two wideouts, as Jaylen Waddle also had a poor showing in his Denver debut, and new offensive coordinator Davis Webb may need to go back to the drawing board quickly to get his passing game going. Sutton should face a softer matchup in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.
outlooksByWeek.4: Courtland Sutton continues to fade into a support role in the Broncos' passing game following the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle. His seven targets in a Week 3 win over the Rams were a season-high, and through three games, he's managed just an 8-82-0 line on 16 total looks from Bo Nix. Sutton should see more volume once new play-caller Davis Webb settles in, but he'll have an uphill battle to produce his fourth career 1,000-yard season. He'll face a 49ers secondary in Week 4 that ranks ninth in fantasy points per game allowed to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: After producing one season with 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish during his first six NFL campaigns, Sutton has achieved both in each of the past two years. The 2018 second-round pick's target share actually dipped from 24% in 2024 to 21% in 2025, but he remained heavily involved near the goal line and has now ranked in the top 12 among receivers in TDs each of the last three seasons. In fact, Sutton has now finished in the top 10 at the position in end zone targets four years in a row, tying for third with 56 during the span. Sutton will remain one of Bo Nix's go-to targets, but now 30 years old and with added target competition in Jaylen Waddle, he's best valued as a fantasy WR3.

outlooksByWeek.2: TreVeyon Henderson could make his season debut in Week 2 when the Patriots host the Steelers. Henderson missed last week due to an ankle injury but has returned to practice ahead of the matchup. Pass-blocking concerns were rumored to be an issue during the preseason, and facing a Steelers defense that rushes the passer well may keep Henderson on the sideline more than managers would like, in addition to a potentially limited role in his first game back. Pittsburgh allowed a mere 3.8 yards per carry in Week 1 but did allow 90 receiving yards to running backs, albeit that was Bijan Robinson. Split touches in a likely low-scoring game would require Henderson's patented big-play ability for him to be fantasy relevant.
outlooksByWeek.3: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.
outlooksByWeek.4: TreVeyon Henderson remains mired in a split backfield for the Patriots ahead of their Week 4 matchup with the Bills. Henderson's snap share dropped from 60% to 35% in Week 3 as the Patriots played from behind, forcing Rhamondre Stevenson into a pass-blocking role. With only one catch through two games, Henderson isn't getting many opportunities to create his signature big play. Facing a defense that's allowing just 3.9 yards per carry while being more vulnerable to receiving backs, Henderson figures to be a boom-or-bust option.

player.seasonOutlook: Henderson enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which he delivered three huge fantasy performances (28-plus points in all three) but otherwise played second fiddle to Rhamondre Stevenson (8.3 points per game in his other 14 games). Though his role was limited, Henderson was effective, averaging 5.1 yards per carry (eighth best) and catching 83% of his targets while scoring 10 touchdowns. The 2025 second-round pick is a candidate for a similar role in 2026, but it's unlikely that Stevenson will completely disappear after he also had a strong 2025. Henderson is safest as a bench option, but there's upside for a lot more if the 23-year-old is promoted to a lead role.

outlooksByWeek.2: Harold Fannin and the Browns visit the Buccaneers in Week 2, facing the 30th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (25.1) to TEs. The second-year pro managed two catches on three targets for 21 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 loss in the season opener. Fannin has the perfect chance at a rebound performance against Tampa Bay, as Cincinnati's Mike Gesicki cooked their defense with five receptions for 78 yards and a TD in Week 1. Even with poor quarterback play, Fannin has the talent and opportunity as the focal point of an offense that might not be good but will be forced to throw the ball plenty while playing from behind.
outlooksByWeek.3: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Harold Fannin Jr. and the Browns host their division rival Steelers in Week 4 for an AFC North clash between two 2-1 teams. He caught seven of nine targets for 51 yards and two TDs during Cleveland's 21-18 victory in Week 3, including the game-winning score. Fannin led the team in receptions and yardage while tying KC Concepcion for first in targets. He now has a 12-126-2 line on 18 targets across three contests as one of Deshaun Watson's favorite receivers. Fannin will have a tough matchup against Pittsburgh's seventh-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.3) to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: Fannin is a rising star at the tight end position after overcoming the presence of David Njoku and a quarterback merry-go-round to produce a 72-731-6 receiving line (plus 7-13-1 rushing) as a 21-year-old rookie last season. The third-round pick's 108 targets rank eighth all time by a rookie tight end, and he finished no lower than eighth at the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and fantasy points last season. Fannin figures to see some touchdown regression (seven TDs, 3.8 expected, three end zone targets) and Cleveland still has quarterback question marks, but with Njoku gone, Fannin has a path to improve a bit on what was already a healthy 22% target share. He's a solid TE1 target.

outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to provide Green Bay's rushing attack while the veteran is absent.

player.seasonOutlook: Jacobs' 2025 season can be split in two parts: pre-injury and post-injury. While healthy during his first nine games, Jacobs picked up where he left off from a terrific 2024 debut season with Green Bay, averaging 21.1 touches and 19.6 fantasy points while scoring 11 TDs. After missing all but 11 snaps during Weeks 11 and 12, Jacobs returned and wasn't quite the same, averaging 14.6 touches and 11.3 points while totaling three touchdowns in his final five games. But Jacobs, 28, was still effective overall (PFF's fourth-highest-graded back) and has a clear grasp on lead-back duties in a good Green Bay offense that has afforded him 30 touchdowns (fifth most in the NFL) in 32 games. He's a fine back-end RB1 when active, but a likely suspension makes him less valuable on draft day.He's worth a mid-round flier until the dust settles.

outlooksByWeek.2: Rashid Shaheed will look to bounce back from a quiet season-opening performance when Seattle visits Arizona in Week 2. Shaheed caught just one of three targets for four yards against New England in Week 1. Drew Lock played most of that game behind center for the Seahawks after Sam Darnold (glute) made an early injury exit, and Lock figures to again lead the offense against Arizona. The Cardinals gave up just 14 points in a surprising victory over the Chargers last weekend, though they did allow Los Angeles' No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey to put up a 5-82-1 line in under three quarters of action before he exited with a rib injury.
outlooksByWeek.3: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Rashid Shaheed has yet to make a big impact in fantasy this season with Seattle's Week 4 matchup against the Chargers coming up. Though Shaheed has been valuable as a return man for the Seahawks, he's averaging just two catches for 17.7 yards through three weeks. Shaheed also fell below a 50% offensive snap share in Week 3 against Washington, as Cooper Kupp served as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind star Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Shaheed may need a big play or two to break out against the Chargers, who have allowed nine receptions of 20-plus yards this season, tied for 13th-most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Shaheed re-signed with Seattle after the team acquired him at last year's trade deadline. Known primarily for his elite return ability, Shaheed made an impact at times as a receiver with New Orleans, but wasn't used much on offense after the trade. In 12 games with the Seahawks (including the playoffs), Shaheed cleared three touches in only two games and averaged 5.9 fantasy PPG. The team's financial investment in Shaheed suggests his role will expand in 2026, but he still has to fend off Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and second-year WR Tory Horton for snaps and targets. Shaheed enters his age-28 season yet to deliver a top-35 fantasy campaign, and he's unlikely to get there this season while also focusing on special teams and working in Seattle's low-pass-volume offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns travel to take on the Buccaneers and their 22nd-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (26.8) to RBs in Week 2. The second-year back rushed 12 times for 33 yards and caught both targets for 17 yards during Cleveland's 34-10 Week 1 loss. Running lanes and beneficial game flow are two things to be concerned with for Judkins, as the Browns again appear to be one of the worst offenses in the league. If the QB play improves even slightly, he could see an uptick in opportunities in both the running and passing games, but he should be started with caution until that situation improves.
outlooksByWeek.3: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Steelers to town for an AFC North clash on Thursday night in Week 4. He rushed 18 times for 70 yards and caught both targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset win over the Panthers in Week 3. Judkins surpassed 35 yards on the ground for the first time this season, and there's a chance he could build upon that against their division rivals. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 20th in fantasy points allowed (22.1) per game to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Judkins is entering his second NFL season after a roller-coaster rookie campaign in which a solid 14-game stretch of action was bookended by missed time early because of an off-field issue and late because of a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. When on the field, Judkins handled a massive 71.4% share of Cleveland's designed rush attempts (16.4 per game). Though he was held to 3.6 yards per carry, he was dealing with a league-high 7.4 box defenders per attempt. He wasn't involved much as a receiver (2.6 targets per game), however, and was limited to 12.1 fantasy points per game (26th among RBs). The Cleveland offense has a new coach (Todd Monken) and quarterback questions remain, so while Judkins has a clear path to a big carry total, the 22-year-old might cap out as a midrange RB2 in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: KC Concepcion and the Browns are on the road in Week 2 to face the Buccaneers and their eighth-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed to WRs (101). The rookie looked hungry and fought for more on every play, catching four of five targets for 43 yards and rushing three times for 15 yards while losing a fumble. Concepcion's blunder came on a play from behind as he tried to gain extra yardage, but it was still a promising debut for the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, as he led the team in receptions and targets. Still, it's difficult to trust anyone on the Browns' offense, especially against a Tampa Bay defense that held Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to 71 combined yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.
outlooksByWeek.4: KC Concepcion and the Browns welcome Pittsburgh to town for an AFC North clash in Week 4. He caught just two of nine targets for nine yards during Cleveland's upset victory in Week 3. Concepcion wasn't able to contribute much despite tying for the team lead in targets with Harold Fannin Jr., but it's still a positive sign that the Browns are looking to get the ball in his hands. He'll get his first chance to face the division-rival Steelers and their 14th-ranked defense in receiving yards allowed (403) to WRs.

player.seasonOutlook: Concepcion was selected by the Browns in the first round of April's draft. He is a quick and explosive short-to-intermediate receiver whose career 27.2% target share topped this entire rookie class. Primarily a slot receiver during his first two seasons at NC State, Concepcion played more on the outside in 2025 at Texas A&M, but he figures to primarily work inside in the pros (career 72% slot rate), while also helping as a rusher and returner. Concepcion will need to fend off the likes of Jerry Jeudy, Harold Fannin Jr. and fellow rookie Denzel Boston for targets in an offense with quarterback issues, so while he has upside, he's best valued as a flex.

The NFL's leading sack-getter the past two seasons, the Broncos D/ST lost DE John Franklin-Myers during the offseason but otherwise return largely the same front for 2026. Led by Zach Allen, Nik Bonitto and four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II, the Broncos scored 15-plus fantasy points on four occasions last season and finished third in the category. Their early-season schedule presents some challenges (@KC, Week 1; LAR, Week 3; @SF, Week 4), but overall theirs is one of the most favorable, especially across a nine-week span beginning in Week 7 (@ARI, KC, @CAR, bye, LV, @PIT, MIA, @NYJ, @LV).

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bucky Irving is expected to operate as the Buccaneers' lead back in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Irving out-touched Kenneth Gainwell 15 to six in the Week 1 loss, which is a very promising sign for his outlook moving forward. The most impressive part about Irving's Week 1 performance was receiving, where he caught all seven of his targets for 48 yards. He could be in for another big week against a Browns defense that allowed 34 points in Week 1. However, Cleveland did give up just 3.9 yards per carry, so Irving may need to continue his success as a receiver for fantasy production.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bucky Irving is expected to remain Tampa Bay's lead back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Irving remained efficient despite the Buccaneers' offensive struggles in Week 2, accounting for 90 total yards on 21 touches. Additionally, he's operated as the clear No. 1 running back, out-touching Kenneth Gainwell 36 to 11 in two contests. Irving will likely struggle in Week 3, however, as he'll be facing a Vikings defense that's allowed just 14.7 PPR fantasy points to RBs this season, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bucky Irving is expected to continue leading the Buccaneers' backfield in the Week 4 matchup against the Packers. Irving was held in check by a strong Vikings defense in Week 3, totaling 58 yards on 17 touches. Despite this inefficient effort, Irving remained the Buccaneers' bell-cow back, as Kenneth Gainwell received just five touches (10 total yards). With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dealing with injury following the Week 3 loss, Irving could see less opportunities through the air. Regardless, Irving's strong workload should bode well for the Week 4 matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed the second-most PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position (30.7) this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Irving enters his third season coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he missed seven games and struggled with efficiency. After averaging 5.42 yards per carry and producing 1,514 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, Irving fell to 3.40 YPC (fourth worst among qualified RBs), 865 yards and four touchdowns in 2025. He failed to clear 4.2 YPC in any of his 10 outings and had zero carries inside the opponent's 5 yard line. The 24-year-old remains positioned as the lead back in Tampa Bay, but the combination of his small frame (5-foot-9, 192 pounds) and the arrival of Kenneth Gainwell (not to mention Sean Tucker at the goal line) suggest he might play a lesser role moving forward. Irving should be valued as a back-end RB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Adonai Mitchell will look to stretch the field for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. Mitchell hauled in all three of his targets to open the year, finishing with 60 yards. Green Bay allowed a mere 7.7 yards per target in Week 1, but that was largely due to facing Carson Wentz for the bulk of the game. Their secondary remains vulnerable and will likely commit multiple bodies to Garrett Wilson, setting up Mitchell for a few plays downfield in single coverage. Mitchell seems likely to continue his low-volume, high-upside role in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.
outlooksByWeek.4: Adonai Mitchell is questionable for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears after missing Week 3 due to a finger injury. Mitchell has been a valuable secondary option opposite Garrett Wilson in his first two games, garnering 15 targets and averaging 13.7 yards per catch. With minimal options behind him and running back Breece Hall (thigh) likely to miss Week 4, Mitchell could have a stable workload against a defense that's allowing 8.5 yards per target to opposing receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Mitchell is entering his first full campaign with the Jets, having been acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade during the 2025 season. After playing sparingly during his first 25 NFL games (all with the Colts), the 2024 second-round pick handled a hefty 24.4% target share in eight games with New York last season. The usage led to two fantasy outings with 17-plus points, but he was otherwise a nonfactor (4.0 PPG). Efficiency remains an issue, as Mitchell's 44% catch rate ranks last, and his 6.0 yards per target is fourth worst among 77 receivers with 100-plus targets since he entered the league. The vertical threat will compete with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. for No. 2 duties opposite a now-healthy Garrett Wilson in the Jets' Geno Smith-led offense. Mitchell, 23, is not worth much more than late-round consideration.

Kirk signed with the 49ers after spending his first eight seasons with Arizona, Jacksonville and Houston. The 2018 second-round pick peaked with a 12th-place finish in fantasy points in 2022, but that marks his only career top-25 finish and he's been way off the fantasy radar the last two seasons, partially due to injury woes (13 missed games). Kirk doesn't have a clear path to consistent targets in San Francisco, with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling also in the mix (not to mention Christian McCaffrey and eventually George Kittle). The 29-year-old will begin the season on IR and is not on the fantasy radar.

The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.
outlooksByWeek.4: Mack Hollins will look to lead the Patriots' receiving corps in Week 4 against the Bills. Hollins gathered a season-high nine targets in Week 3, following just seven total in the team's first two games, as the Patriots continue to search for a top option without A.J. Brown (ankle) available. Drake Maye is struggling to move this offense, but Week 4 offers the potential to match the Bills' high-scoring offense. Buffalo is allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers and an enticing 9.2 yards per target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Fitzgerald is in for a favorable Week 2 matchup when the Panthers face the Falcons, who gave up 8.0 kicking points in a Week 1 loss. Fitzgerald made five of his six kicks last week, drilling his only field-goal attempt while going four-for-five on point-after tries. He's expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 2, as he averaged 11.0 kicking points per game in two games against Atlanta in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Fitzgerald is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Fitzgerald has started the season strong, converting on all three of his field-goal tries and eight of nine point-after attempts. Additionally, he could continue to benefit from the Panthers' offensive success, as the team currently ranks second in points per game (35.5). Fitzgerald is in for a great Week 3 matchup as well, with Cleveland allowing 11.5 kicking points per game through two contests this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Ryan Fitzgerald will look to continue building on an impressive performance in the Panthers' Week 4 matchup against the Lions. Fitzgerald was perfect in Carolina's Week 3 loss, converting on all four of his field-goal tries. On the season, he's made all seven field-goal attempts and eight of nine point-after tries. Fitzgerald expected to continue seeing plenty of scoring opportunities in Week 4, as Detroit's defense has allowed 31.7 points per game this season, despite giving up just 5.0 kicking points per game.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathan Taylor carried the Colts' offense with 121 scrimmage yards and two TDs on 22 touches in the season opener. His heavy Week 1 workload was encouraging considering the Colts trailed by 18 points at halftime and lost by that same margin to the Ravens. Indianapolis could face another negative game script in Week 2 at Kansas City, but Taylor remains locked in as a fantasy RB1, even with the team around him looking shaky. Taylor led the NFL with 323 carries and 18 rushing TDs last season while compiling 1,963 scrimmage yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jonathan Taylor has four rushing TDs through three games and is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 game against the Commanders in London. Washington has allowed the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL while struggling to defend the pass, but the Colts have proven they intend to feed their star RB a steady diet of carries regardless of opponent. A positive game script is certainly possible against a Commanders team that's starting backup QB Marcus Mariota, so Taylor has a clear path to another heavy workload and remains a must-start fantasy option.

player.seasonOutlook: Taylor enters the 2026 season having improved in fantasy points per game in each of the past three years. Last season, he delivered his best production since his huge 2021 campaign, as he paced the NFL in carries and TDs while finishing second in carries inside the 5-yard line (19) and fourth in fantasy points. A piece of the step forward was increased usage in the passing game, as he ranked in the top 10 among backs in routes, targets, catches and receiving yards, setting career highs in each. Taylor's season likely would've been even better had QB Daniel Jones not been injured, as the running back averaged 24.8 points with Jones but 12.9 without him. Jones is expected to be ready to play in Week 1, so the 27-year-old Taylor is safe to value as a mid- to high-end RB1.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omarion Hampton looked like the clear lead back for the Chargers in their season-opening loss to the Cardinals, taking 12 carries for 43 yards and a touchdown, while backup Keaton Mitchell saw only four carries. Neither RB caught a pass as Justin Herbert had a very narrow target tree under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, connecting with just five different receivers. Hampton had been headed for a big rookie campaign before getting injured, so staying healthy will be the biggest factor in any potential 2026 breakout. He could post better numbers in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that ranked 21st last season in points per game allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.
outlooksByWeek.4: Omarion Hampton's workload took a step backward in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, as the Chargers' backfield teeters toward a committee. The second-year back hasn't been awful, producing 214 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in three games while averaging 3.9 yards per carry, but Keaton Mitchell is averaging 5.0 yards per carry on limited usage and may be a better fit for offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Kimani Vidal also had his first touches of the season in Buffalo. Hampton is the most talented player of the three on paper, but with the 0-3 Chargers struggling to generate offense, every possible solution will be on the table. He isn't likely to start turning things around in Week 4 against a Seahawks defense that ranks fifth in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Hampton is primed for a breakout second season following an impressive but injury-shortened rookie campaign. The first-round pick was busy during nine appearances, averaging 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets. He scored five touchdowns, averaged 15.1 fantasy points per game (13th best) and ranked third among backs in forced missed tackle rate, per PFF. With Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell as his primary competition, Hampton has a clear path to lead rusher duties in 2026, and his targets only figure to increase with Greg Roman out and Mike McDaniel in as the team's playcaller. Add in a much-improved offensive line with star tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back healthy, and Hampton has nothing short of elite upside. Value him as a fringe RB1 with room for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drake London looks poised to bounce back from a tough Week 1 in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina's defense just allowed a whopping 59 points to the Bears in Week 1, giving up 42.2 PPR fantasy points to wide receivers. London's rebound could depend on the quarterback play, as Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) are both questionable for Sunday's contest. However, with Carolina's defensive struggles during Week 1, London should be in for a fantastic matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.4: Drake London will look to stay hot in the Falcons' Week 4 matchup against the Saints. With Michael Penix returning from injury in the Week 3 win over the Packers, London had one of the best performances of his career, catching nine of 10 targets for 194 yards. With Penix on the field, London has averaged 6.7 receptions, 98.7 receiving yards and 0.6 touchdowns per game, suggesting he'll remain one of fantasy's top wideouts as long as Penix remains healthy. Despite this, London is in for a tough Week 4 matchup against a Saints secondary that's given up 29.0 PPR fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts this season.

player.seasonOutlook: London enters his fifth NFL season with eyes on finishing in the top 15 in fantasy points per game for the third season in a row. The 2022 first-round pick broke out with a 100-1,271-9 receiving line and a fifth-place finish in fantasy points (14th PPG) in 2024. Last season, he missed five games and fell to 19th in fantasy points, but he was actually better on a per-game basis (seventh) and was the top scorer among receivers three times between Weeks 6 and 10. London remains heavily targeted (career 28% share) and sees plenty of work near the goal line (25 end zone targets over the past two seasons). As long as one of Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. can play somewhat competent ball, the 25-year-old London shouldn't have trouble providing fringe-WR1 fantasy production.

outlooksByWeek.2: Travis Etienne is expected to remain New Orleans' top running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Despite Alvin Kamara (knee) being sidelined for the Week 1 overtime loss, Etienne only received nine carries, tying Kendre Miller for the most on the team. However, Etienne was busy as a receiver, catching seven of nine targets for 46 yards, which is a positive sign for his fantasy outlook going forward. He could be in for another productive week, as Baltimore's defense allowed 28.1 PPR fantasy points to running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Etienne signed with the Saints after spending the first five seasons of his pro career with the Jaguars. The 2021 first-round pick has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. A capable rusher and receiver, Etienne has already reached 1,000-plus rushing yards three times and has 35-plus catches in each of the past four seasons. Even if the Saints retain Alvin Kamara as a situational player, Etienne will have a clear path to feature-back duties in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough. That will be enough to position the 27-year-old for his third top-15 fantasy campaign in four years. Consider Etienne a solid RB2 target with backend RB1 upside.

outlooksByWeek.2: Garrett Wilson should maintain steady volume for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers. He garnered seven targets in a run-heavy situation to open the year, catching six for 79 yards. Green Bay's secondary is suspect and just allowed Vikings' top receiver Justin Jefferson to score twice, despite Carson Wentz being under center. The Jets will likely need to throw more in Week 2, potentially pushing Wilson into double-digit targets and setting him up for elevated numbers.
outlooksByWeek.3: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.
outlooksByWeek.4: Garrett Wilson likely remains a heavily targeted option for the Jets in Week 4 against the Bears. Wilson is coming off a terrific 10-catch, 107-yard Week 3 where he scored his first touchdown of the season and faces minimal competition for volume in the Jets' passing game. Chicago's secondary has rallied over the last two weeks, not allowing more than 153 yards through the air, but the pieces at corner leave plenty to be desired, setting Wilson up to take advantage of continued high looks in Week 4.

player.seasonOutlook: Wilson is eyeing a bounce-back following an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games. It was the first time Wilson had missed time, having appeared in all 51 games during his first three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick ranked no lower than sixth among receivers in targets in each of those years, but he failed to produce a fantasy campaign better than 20th (PPG) due to New York's quarterback woes. Wilson was off to a hot start last season (four TDs, 14.2 fantasy PPG) thanks to a massive 33% target share (second highest). New York's signal-caller problems still aren't completely solved, but veteran Geno Smith should provide an upgrade over last year's Justin Fields/Tyrod Taylor duo. Wilson, 26, is one of the best raw talents at the position and should be valued as a good WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: DJ Moore will look to build on an impressive debut when the Bills host the Lions in Week 2. Despite new quarterback Josh Allen continuing to spread the ball around, Moore popped with a 100-yard outing on eight targets. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to open the year, but just 7.3 yards per attempt as New Orleans was forced to throw from behind. That may not be the case Thursday, and Moore is unlikely to garner high volume. Even so, facing a secondary void of high-end talent, Moore can get deep and provide big yardage without a lot of opportunity.
outlooksByWeek.3: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.
outlooksByWeek.4: DJ Moore aims to remain heavily involved in the Bills' Week 4 game against the Patriots. In two healthy games, Moore has 18 targets as Josh Allen's top option, creating a stable floor. New England's secondary is middling, allowing the 18th-most fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, no one has topped 64 yards against them. Moore's potential could be further capped if he draws shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.

player.seasonOutlook: Moore was traded to Buffalo after spending his first eight NFL seasons with Carolina and Chicago. A featured target throughout most of his career, Moore was reduced to a 16% target share in 2025 -- his lowest since his rookie year in 2018. The result was a 35th-place finish in fantasy points, which ended a streak of six consecutive top 25s. Moore now heads to Buffalo with Khalil Shakir as his only roadblock to emerging as Josh Allen's No. 1 target in Buffalo's high-scoring offense. Still in his prime at age 29, Moore has the look of a fantasy WR3 with upside for more.

outlooksByWeek.2: Parker Washington can safely be started as a fantasy WR2 in Week 2, even with the Jaguars facing a stout Broncos secondary. Washington paced Jacksonville's pass catchers with five catches for 83 yards and a TD on six targets in the season opener. In his last five games, including the playoffs, Washington has racked up 31 catches, 537 yards, and four TDs. Fellow Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) tends to draw significant defensive attention, which should keep top Broncos CB Patrick Surtain from shadowing Washington as long as Thomas suits up.
outlooksByWeek.3: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.
outlooksByWeek.4: Parker Washington has entered set-and-forget fantasy WR1 territory. Jacksonville's top wideout is likely to thrive in Week 4 against a suspect Bengals secondary that just allowed touchdowns to Steelers WRs Roman Wilson, DK Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek. Despite facing the strong Cleveland, Denver, and New England secondaries, Washington is averaging 74 yards per game with two TDs through three weeks to start 2026 after averaging 116 receiving yards and scoring twice in the final three games of the 2025 regular season.

player.seasonOutlook: A strong finish to the 2025 season has made Washington one of the fascinating breakout candidates of 2026. Though he's primarily worked as a situational/depth player since being drafted in the sixth round in 2023, Washington has flashed when asked to play a bigger role. In 21 games since the start of 2024 in which he had a route participation above 50%, Washington handled a 20% target share and averaged 12.2 fantasy PPG. He surprisingly emerged as Jacksonville's top target late last season, which included a stretch of four straight games with at least nine targets and 19 fantasy points to end the season. The 24-year-old appears to have cemented a big role in Jacksonville, though Jakobi Meyers, Brian Thomas Jr. and perhaps Travis Hunter will battle him for snaps and targets. Washington should be targeted for your flex spot.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jonathon Brooks is expected to operate as Carolina's No. 2 running back in the Week 2 matchup against the Falcons. Brooks received just four carries in the Week 1 loss, which is fewer than Chuba Hubbard (10) and AJ Dillon (five). However, all of Dillon's work came when the Panthers were down substantially in the fourth quarter. Brooks showed flashes of brilliance when on the field, most notably on a 48-yard catch and run. He could continue to take work from Hubbard as the season continues. However, he's in for a tough Week 2 matchup, with Atlanta allowing just 2.8 yards per rush attempt in Week 1, the best mark in the NFL.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Brooks is considered week-to-week after tweaking the same groin he first injured during training camp in the Week 2 win over the Falcons. Prior to his injury, the Texas product was clearly operating as Carolina's second RB, tallying just nine carries for 30 yards and two catches for 43 yards over the team's first two contests. Brooks will likely to find fantasy relevance if active in Week 3, with Cleveland's defense allowing just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Brooks is hoping to get his career on track in 2026 after appearing in only one game since being drafted in the second round of the 2024 draft. Brooks spent most of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL suffered while at the University of Texas. He returned in Week 12 and handled 12 touches in three games prior to retearing the same ACL and missing the entire 2025 season. Only 23 years old and skilled as a rusher and receiver, Brooks figures to eventually get his shot at a lead-back role in the pros. He's expected to battle for touches with Chuba Hubbard this season, so it's possible he quickly earns his way into a fantasy-relevant role. Consider him in the middle rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Wilson will look to break through against a tough Seattle secondary for Arizona in Week 2. Wilson performed well in a season-opening win over the Chargers, catching five of seven targets for 56 yards. He outproduced presumed No. 1 wideout Marvin Harrison, though newcomer Kendrick Bourne led the WR corps with an 8-75-0 line. All three figure to be challenged by a Seahawks defense that ranked 10th in passing yards allowed last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Wilson faces a tough challenge in Arizona's Week 3 matchup in San Francisco. Wilson was quiet against Seattle this past Sunday, catching just two of seven targets for 18 yards. However, he was still the Cardinals' second-leading receiver in a game during which QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards. The 49ers have surrendered only 15.6 fantasy points per game to wideouts, the ninth-best mark in the league threw two weeks.
outlooksByWeek.4: Michael Wilson appears to be Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite wideout target heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Giants. Wilson got a whopping 17 targets this past Sunday in a loss to San Francisco, recording 11 catches for 89 yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison posted a quiet 3-40-0 line on five targets. Of course, star TE Trey McBride will consistently draw plenty of Brissett's attention, but it looks like Wilson is in line for lots of looks in the team's offense. He could thrive against a Giants defense that is giving up 23.6 fantasy points per game to WRs, ninth-most in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game during his first 38 NFL games, Wilson broke out with Jacoby Brissett under center during the final eight games of 2025, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy PPG. The stretch also coincided with Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with health issues, and it's worth noting that Wilson's receiving lines in the four games Harrison was active weren't quite as good (3-40-0, 3-61-0, 4-34-0, 3-36-0). A healthy Harrison (along with TE Trey McBride) figures to lead to a return to earth for Wilson, but the 26-year-old did enough late last season to warrant WR4/flex consideration in drafts.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joe Burrow and the Bengals travel to take on the Texans in Week 2. Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards with one TD and one INT, and he rushed five times for 20 yards in their season-opening win. Houston ranks 28th in fantasy points allowed per game (39.0) to QBs after Josh Allen torched them for 357 scrimmage yards and four TDs. Burrow will look to get Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins more involved after the receivers combined for 71 yards on just five catches.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on the road to face the Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with back spasms in practice, Burrow was a full go in Week 2, throwing for 207 yards (20-for-31) with two TDs and no INTs in the 20-6 victory. He faces a stout Pittsburgh defense that ranks first in fantasy points allowed (11.6) to QBs and seventh in passing yards allowed. Burrow is one of the best at his position, but fantasy managers should approach this matchup with caution after the Steelers held Drake Maye to 208 passing yards (14-for-22) with one pick while sacking him three times in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.4: Joe Burrow and the Bengals host the Jaguars for a battle between 2-1 teams in Week 4. He threw for 282 yards (28-for-37) with three TDs and no INTs and added 13 yards on two carries during Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Week 3. Burrow also lost a fumble in the final minute of the contest, but he had a strong outing overall against a tough defense. Up next is another difficult task, as Jacksonville's defense is tied for fifth, allowing 16.8 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Burrow will attempt to bounce back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025. The 29-year-old has now missed at least six games in three of his six pro seasons, including two of his past three. Burrow was still a starting-caliber fantasy quarterback when active last season (top-12 scorer in five of his final six games), but his ceiling was limited by a near complete lack of rushing (41 yards on 14 carries). Burrow was a top-five scoring quarterback in each of his past two full seasons, and coach Zac Taylor cut back a bit on his extreme pass-heavy playcalling last season, so Burrow is best valued as more of a midrange QB1 than an elite option.

outlooksByWeek.2: J.K. Dobbins wasn't a big part of the Broncos' game plan in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, as the veteran running back had only eight carries for 36 yards. RJ Harvey's volume was similar, with seven touches to Dobbins' eight, but turnovers and game flow played a part in limiting their opportunities. Dobbins averaged over 80 scrimmage yards last season in the 10 regular-season games he was healthy, so better days should be ahead for Denver's lead back, although they may not come right away. In Week 2, he'll face a Jaguars defense that ranked third in points per game allowed to RBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.
outlooksByWeek.4: J.K. Dobbins is coming off his largest workload of the season in the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams. He had 17 carries and 18 total touches but turned them into just 53 scrimmage yards. Dobbins has struggled out of the gate, averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, but he should continue to handle the majority of the early-down work while rookie Jonah Coleman is on IR. RJ Harvey, who compiled 47 scrimmage yards on just eight touches against the Rams, remains the primary passing-down back. Dobbins will look for his first touchdown of 2026 in Week 4 against a 49ers defense that ranks 22nd in fantasy points per game allowed to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Dobbins re-signed with Denver and will attempt to fend off sophomore RJ Harvey for the team's lead-back job. With both active during Weeks 1-10 last season (10 games), Dobbins handled 153 carries (60% team share) and 15 targets (4%), compared to 50 carries (20%) and 29 targets (9%) for Harvey. Dobbins ran well (5.05 yards per carry) when healthy, but he was limited to four touchdowns and was a nonfactor as a receiver (37 yards on 15 targets) en route to averaging 11.6 fantasy points (27th). Dobbins enters his age-27 campaign having yet to play a full season in his career (seven-plus missed games in four of the past five years) and without much value even when active (he has never produced a top-20 fantasy campaign). Dobbins is an underwhelming flex option with added value in non-PPR formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colston Loveland will look to get more involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Loveland disappointed in Week 1 against the Panthers, failing to bring in either of his two targets, even though it was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The second-year tight end's output was hopefully a fluke, especially as he was still on the field for 86 percent of Chicago's offensive snaps. Loveland will also face a Minnesota defense that allowed five catches for 115 yards to Green Bay's tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).
outlooksByWeek.4: Colston Loveland will look to improve his role even more as the Bears play the Jets in Week 4. Loveland finally saw more than a chalked role against the Eagles in Week 3, reeling in all four of his targets for 31 yards. This output is far from what was expected of the second-year tight end heading into the season, but it's still optimistic for the future. He'll face a New York defense that's ceded a top-ten 8.0 fantasy points per game to TEs.

player.seasonOutlook: After averaging 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy PPG during his first 14 NFL games, Loveland leaped to 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 fantasy PPG during his final four games of 2025 (including the playoffs). For perspective, there have been only 12 instances of a tight end seeing at least 10 targets in four consecutive regular-season games in NFL history (and only one was a rookie). Loveland's overall efficiency was terrific, as he ranked eighth or better among tight ends in YPR, YPT and YPRR. With DJ Moore gone, the 2025 first-round pick enters his age-22 season all but locked into a massive workload alongside Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Loveland's ceiling is lofty, and midrange fantasy TE1 should be his floor.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Likely scored twice in his debut for the Giants in Week 1, leading a stunning victory over the Cowboys. Likely caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and the two scores to lead the Giants in receiving. Especially in the red zone and on third down, quarterback Jaxson Dart leaned heavily on his new tight end, something that should continue in Week 2 versus the Rams. Los Angeles allowed 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in its dismal season-opening loss to the 49ers, while also losing star acquisition Myles Garrett to a knee injury. Aaron Donald will make his return from retirement to help out the defensive line, though.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Likely led the Giants in both receptions and targets last game. Despite seeing 10 opportunities, though, Likely caught five passes for just 33 yards in the dismal loss to the Rams. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Likely will likely see his stock take a hit. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.4: Isaiah Likely's breakout season likely came to a crashing halt with the injury to Jaxson Dart. Likely managed just two catches for 13 yards in the win over the Titans last game. Jameis Winston has been uninspiring to say the least at quarterback, which has limited the opportunities for Likely.  Winston should remain under center in Week 4 versus a vulnerable Cardinals defense. Arizona is allowing 234.3 passing yards per game, which is 22nd in the NFL. In addition, Arizona has allowed eight passing touchdowns already, which is 30th in the league.

player.seasonOutlook: Likely signed with the Giants after four years of backing up Mark Andrews in Baltimore. Likely is reuniting with coach John Harbaugh and is finally expected to play a consistent offensive role. During his time in Baltimore, Likely was limited to 50% of the team's offensive snaps and never finished a season better than 20th among tight ends in snaps, routes, targets, catches, yards or fantasy PPG. His only extensive stretch with Andrews sidelined came back in 2023. During the seven-game span, Likely posted a 23-356-6 receiving line on a 16% target share and averaged a solid 13.5 fantasy PPG. The 26-year-old is obviously unproven, but his receiving skills in New York's ascending offense are enough to put him on the TE2 radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Malik Washington hopes for more efficiency when the Dolphins face the 49ers in Week 2. Washington recorded a healthy eight targets in the team's opener, and while 17.7 yards per catch is encouraging, he caught only three balls. Washington has value as a returner in some leagues, and passing volume will likely remain high with Miami forced to throw from behind in the second half. Even so, Week 2's matchup against a defense that held more talented receivers to just 6.4 yards per target in their opener is a risky endeavor.
outlooksByWeek.3: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.
outlooksByWeek.4: Malik Washington remains heavily involved in the Dolphins' low-profile passing game heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. Washington is coming off of a season-high 10 targets in Week 3, and has collected three rushing attempts over the last two weeks while also being involved in kickoff returns, but he's yet to top 61 rushing/receiving yards per game or score. Washington's workload creates a viable floor, and Minnesota is allowing a healthy 8.2 yards per target to opposing receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Washington was a sixth-round flier back in 2024, but that didn't stop him from working his way into a substantial offensive role last season. Washington finished third on the Dolphins in targets, trailing only Jaylen Waddle and De'Von Achane. Of course, Miami's shaky group of offensive personnel was an obvious factor and Washington's efficiency wasn't very good (5.0 yards per target, 7.0 yards per reception, 0.9 yards per route run). The 25-year-old is fine as a short-range target and occasional rusher, but that's likely his ceiling with newcomers Jalen Tolbert, Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. expected to factor in at wide receiver.

Tyson was selected by the Saints with the No. 8 overall pick of April's draft. He is a versatile receiver with decent size who led this rookie class with a 35% target share during the nine weeks he was active in 2025. Injuries cost him time during all four collegiate seasons, but he still managed a 158-2,282-22 receiving line in 33 games, posting a strong 2.73 YPRR along the way (third best in this class). Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August and will miss a month or two of the regular season prior to taking over as the Saints' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave. Once healthy, Tyson has a path to a substantial role in an ascending offense led by second-year QB Tyler Shough and could find himself on the WR3 radar. Of course, with the injury, he's only worth a late flier.

Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Bates will aim to stay perfect as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. Bates nailed his only field-goal attempt and all four extra points against the Saints in Week 1. The third-year player led all NFL kickers in PATs last season in Detroit's high-powered offense, so he'll hopefully stay on the field plenty in the coming weeks. Given that the Bills' defense should provide more problems for the Lions, Bates could also get more field-goal shots in what could be a tough away matchup.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Bates will seek to stay perfect as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Bates has now drilled both of his two field-goal attempts and all eight of his PATs this season. The third-year kicker hasn't been on the field for many field goals this season, and Detroit playing from behind doesn't help his case. Luckily, the team's current high volume of touchdowns has kept Bates relevant. He'll face a New York squad that's allowed 6.0 points per game to kickers across two games, a top-10 mark.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jake Bates will look to stay perfect as the Lions play the Panthers in Week 4. Bates nailed his sole extra-point attempt and all four of his XPAs in Week 3 against the Jets. The third-year boot has now converted all three of his field-goal kicks and each of his 12 extra-point tries. While the field-goal volume isn't quite there, Detroit's ability to score keeps Bates on the field and scoring. Carolina has allowed a middle-of-the-pack 7.0 points per game to kickers this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Love should continue to lead a high-volume passing attack as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Love finished Week 1 with the second-highest passing yard total of his career (387), completing 21 of 42 passes with two touchdowns and one interception. Most of his success came in the first half, with then two turnovers and virtually no offensive prowess in the fourth quarter. With that being said, Green Bay should continue to rely on the passing offense, especially given that there's no return timeline for RB1 Josh Jacobs (personal). Given that Love was able to find success against one of the best defenses in the game, he should have no problem piecing up a New York unit that allowed the seventh-most fantasy points per game (22.1) to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Love will look to make a statement as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Love snuck out a win for Green Bay in Week 2, but a 55.2 percent completion rate for 145 yards, even with a 2:0 TD:INT, was uninspiring against the Jets. The sixth-year gunslinger luckily still sits at 532 passing yards on the year with four touchdowns and one interception, and his high volume only looks to continue with Josh Jacobs' return date uncertain. He'll face an Atlanta defense that gave up 287 passing yards and three touchdowns to Bryce Young this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.4: Jordan Love will look to get the Packers back in the win column against Tampa Bay in Week 4. Love posted friendly fantasy numbers in Week 3 even amidst a disappointing loss, completing 52.8 percent of passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. The sixth-year quarterback has now thrown two touchdowns in every game so far this season, and he's eclipsed 300 passing yards twice. Love remains a solid, high-volume option moving forward, especially given the struggles of Green Bay's run game. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a top-10 18.3 fantasy points per game to QBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Love is back for his fourth season as the Packers' starting quarterback. The 2020 first-round pick has emerged as one of the league's best passers (he has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR during his three seasons as a starter), but that hasn't converted to much fantasy production as of late. After finishing sixth in fantasy points per game in 2023, Love has finished 17th and 21st the past two seasons. A dramatic dip in both passing (19th in pass attempts both years) and rushing (282 yards and one TD total during the two seasons) has been the culprit. Love, who produced just five weekly finishes better than 16th last season, has a limited ceiling in Matt LaFleur's scheme. He's best valued as a back-end QB2.

outlooksByWeek.4: Despite not recording a touch to date, Isaiah Davis could have meaningful touches in Week 4 when the Jets face the Bears. Breece Hall (thigh) seems unlikely to play, elevating Braelon Allen to the lead back role with Davis as a secondary option. Allen hasn't shouldered a heavy load his entire career, having double-digit carries just three times, all during his rookie 2024 season. The Bears are allowing a generous 4.9 yards per carry, so even a handful of rushes for Davis could yield positive results.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bijan Robinson will continue to lead Atlanta's offense in a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Panthers. Robinson received a whopping 29 touches in Week 1, tying Ashton Jeanty for the second-most in the NFL. The Texas product looked explosive despite the Falcons' offensive struggles, which is a good sign for his outlook going forward. Robinson is in for a great matchup as well, with the Panthers defense allowing 291 rushing yards and six rushing touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.
outlooksByWeek.4: Bijan Robinson is expected to continue being the main playmaker on the Falcons' offense in the Week 4 matchup against the Saints. Robinson has been stellar despite Atlanta's offensive struggles three weeks into the season, accounting for 467 total yards and three touchdowns. He's already recorded 79 touches (26.3 per game) this year, suggesting this massive fantasy output will continue as the season progresses. Additionally, Robinson is in for a favorable Week 4 matchup against a Saints defense that's allowed 27.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the RB position.

player.seasonOutlook: Robinson enters his fourth season having finished in the top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons. Also a big factor as a receiver, he has ranked no lower than fifth at the position in routes, targets, receptions and receiving yards in his three pro seasons. In 2025, PFF tracked him with 86 forced missed tackles, which was easily the most among backs. The 24-year-old is in his prime and, though he has a new coach in Kevin Stefanski, his path to a massive offensive role remains clear. He's on the short list of players who should be considered with the first pick of your fantasy draft.

outlooksByWeek.2: Trey McBride marches into a Week 2 matchup versus Seattle fresh off a strong season-opening performance in Arizona's victory against the Chargers. McBride led Cardinals pass catchers across the board with nine catches, 13 targets and 95 yards in that win, and he scored the team's lone passing touchdown. The All-Pro is essentially matchup-proof as possibly the league's premier tight end, though he'll draw a tough Seahawks defense in Week 2. However, it's worth noting that Seattle gave up the sixth-most receiving yards to tight ends during the regular season last year.
outlooksByWeek.3: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: Trey McBride will look to continue a strong start to the campaign when the Cardinals face the Giants in Week 4. McBride posted a 9-75-0 receiving line in a Week 3 loss to San Francisco, though he didn't get into the end zone for the first time this season. The All-Pro has now logged at least eight catches and at least 10 targets in every contest so far in 2026, giving him the highest floor of any TE in the NFL. The Giants rank in the bottom 10 leaguewide in catch rate and receiving yards allowed to tight ends, so they don't figure to be a threat to McBride's run of success.

player.seasonOutlook: McBride has emerged as one of the league's top pass catchers -- not just tight ends -- as he trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons and is sixth in receiving yards (2,385). McBride led the tight end position in every fantasy-relevant counting stat in 2025, and his league-high 15 top-12 fantasy weeks were six more than any other player at the position. He finished third in the NFL with 17 end zone targets. McBride really thrived when Jacoby Brissett (21.1 PPG) replaced Kyler Murray (12.5) under center, which only adds to his 2026 appeal. The 26-year-old should be on your radar at the first-/second-round turn.
